item.title: Harnessing Technological Innovation for Managing Volatility and Advancing Sustainable and Regenerative Supply Chains
item.content:encoded:
Md Maruf Hossan Chowdhury, University of Technology Sydney

Shahriar Akter, University of Wollongong

Mohammad Alamgir Hossain, RMIT University

Kristijan Mirkovski, Deakin University

Supply chains face escalating disruptions from climate change, geopolitical instability, pandemics, and regulatory pressures, while stakeholders increasingly demand sustainable and ethical practices. Digital technologies such as AI, blockchain, IoT, and advanced analytics are transforming supply chain operations by enhancing visibility and enabling data-driven decision-making that can address both resilience and sustainability goals.

This special issue seeks to explore how digital innovation integrates sustainability and resilience in supply chains while identifying gaps between current research and practice. Contributions should address theoretical and empirical questions about when and how technologies support or constrain environmental and social performance, considering contextual factors like institutional environments and geopolitical dynamics, as well as emerging issues such as circular economy transitions and sovereign artificial intelligence.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Logistics Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Emerging digital technologies (e.g., AI, IoT, blockchain) for sustainability and resilience in supply chain management
  • Data-driven decarbonisation strategies and emissions transparency in logistics management
  • Digital enablers of circular supply chains, reverse logistics, and closed-loop systems
  • Digital transformation, resilience, and sustainable supply chain risk management
  • Technology-enabled supply chain resilience capabilities and competitive advantage
  • Blockchain-based traceability, transparency, and ethical sourcing in supply chain management
  • Digital product passports and lifecycle data integration
  • Governance, ethics, data integrity, and cybersecurity in digital supply chain management
  • Institutional and regulatory influences on technology-led sustainability initiatives in supply chain management
  • Digital platforms for supplier sustainability assessment and collaboration
  • Techno-nationalism, sovereign AI, and implications for managing global supply chains
  • Theoretical perspectives on technology-sustainability-resilience linkages in supply chain management
  • Integrating theory and practice in technology-led regenerative practices in supply chains

Timeline

  • September 15, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • March 15, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Resilient, Inclusive and Digital Supply Chains for Africa's Sustainable Development
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines how supply chains can better support Africa's sustainable development by strengthening resilience to disruptions, promoting inclusivity for local communities, and harnessing digital technologies including artificial intelligence. The collection seeks interdisciplinary contributions from academics, practitioners, and policymakers addressing digital transformation, risk management, sustainability, and sector-specific applications in areas like healthcare and agribusiness.

The issue emphasizes rigorous, peer-reviewed research that combines theoretical rigor with practical insights, fosters collaboration across disciplines, and identifies best practices and innovative frameworks for building robust and equitable supply chain systems across Africa.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Logistics Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Building resilient and risk-responsive supply chains: Examining strategies for managing disruptions, strengthening adaptive capacity, and improving crisis preparedness in volatile and resource-constrained environments.
  • Inclusive supply chain models for local economic participation: Investigating approaches that integrate SMEs, informal sectors, and local communities into value chains to promote equitable development.
  • Sustainable and green supply chain practices: Analysing environmentally responsible logistics, circular economy approaches, and sustainable production and consumption systems across key African sectors.
  • Artificial intelligence and digital transformation in African supply chains: Exploring AI, data-driven decision-making, and digital platforms to enhance efficiency, transparency, and responsiveness in supply chain operations.
  • Sector-specific innovations in critical industries: Focusing on applications in healthcare, agribusiness, and other strategic sectors to demonstrate context-specific solutions for development impact.

Timeline

  • December 31, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • January 29, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: A Systemic Understanding of Supply Chain Resilience: Cross-Level Interactions, Multi-Level Frameworks, and Theoretical Innovations
item.content:encoded:
Guoqing Zhao, Swansea University

Samuel Fosso Wamba, TBS Business School

Maciel M. Queiroz, FGV EAESP

Over the last decade, supply chains have been repeatedly disrupted by large-scale shocks, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, geographical conflicts (e.g., Russia-Ukraine war, US-China trade tensions), and climate change-related disasters such as the 2021 Henan floods and the 2024 Spanish floods. These events have illustrated how disturbances at one level can cascade across other levels, leading to systemic failure.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Logistics Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Conceptualizing supply chain resilience as a multi-level framework
  • Integrating individual, organizational, supply chain, and environmental levels to develop a systemic and multi-level understanding of supply chain resilience
  • Advancing a systemic perspective by conceptualizing supply chain resilience as a form of socio-ecological resilience or socio-technological resilience
  • Developing a contextualized understanding of supply chain resilience by examining how it manifests across different environments, such as diverse cultural, institutional, and geographical settings
  • Investigating how individual-level factors, such as personal traits, leadership styles, and managerial cognition, influence the implementation of supply chain resilience strategies
  • Mechanisms by which resilience at one level influences (or conflicts with) resilience at another
  • Applying and extending theoretical frameworks such as systems theory, socio-technological theory, panarchy theory, and middle-range theory in the area of supply chain resilience
  • Developing new models or frameworks that explain supply chain resilience as an emergent system property
  • How digital platforms, AI, IoT, blockchain, and digital twins mediate resilience interactions across individuals, organizational and supply chain levels
  • Tools, frameworks, and capabilities that managers can use to align resilience actions across organizational boundaries
  • Balancing efficiency, flexibility, and redundancy across different levels of the supply chain

Timeline

  • June 1, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • October 1, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Essay Frontiers: A Call for Bold Ideas, New Voices, and New Directions in Logistics and SCM
item.content:encoded:
Maciel Queiroz, FGV EAESP

Morgane Fritz, Excelia Business School

Britta Gammelgaard, University of Southern Denmark

Logistics and supply chain management (L/SCM) have advanced through analytical rigor and empirical refinement. However, the contemporary landscape, shaped by geopolitical shifts, digital transformation, climate pressures, and evolving societal expectations, requires more than incremental extensions of existing models. It calls for a reconsideration of the assumptions, values, and conceptual boundaries that underpin the field. Many of the most pressing challenges in L/SCM today are not only empirical, but also normative, philosophical, and inherently interdisciplinary.

This special issue seeks essays that move beyond established paradigms and offer reflective, provocative, and conceptually grounded perspectives that offer new lenses and open new directions for research and practice. The objective is to complement empirical work by fostering ideas that challenge, reframe, and extend our understanding of L/SCM.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Logistics Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Algorithmic management and the reconfiguration of work in logistics
  • Supply chains as political and strategic infrastructures
  • Entrepreneurial supply chains in contexts of institutional fragility
  • Efficiency versus dignity: ethical boundaries of automation
  • Decolonizing supply chain theory and practice
  • Beyond resilience: strategic adaptation, transformation, and fragility
  • Platformization and ecosystem competition in logistics
  • Invisible labor and precarity in digitally mediated supply chains
  • Sustainability, legitimacy, and organizational narratives
  • The role of human resources in supply chain management
  • Temporal trade-offs: speed, flexibility, and human well-being
  • Culture, identity, and coordination in global supply networks
  • Human–AI collaboration and decision authority in SCM
  • Moral responsibility and accountability in complex supply networks
  • Business model innovation in circular and regenerative supply chains
  • Reimagining SCM theory: integration, borrowing, or paradigm shift?

Timeline

  • September 30, 2026: Closing date for abstract submissions
  • November 30, 2026: Opening date for manuscript submissions
